title: Odd Even Linked List
statement: Group nodes with odd 1-based indices before nodes with even indices, preserving relative order inside each group. The input is the value sequence. Rewire next pointers rather than building the answer by index arithmetic alone.
hints: Keep an odd tail and an even head and even tail.
Weave: odd.next = even.next, then advance odd. even.next = odd.next, then advance even.
Finally connect the odd tail to the even head.
editorial: If the list has fewer than two nodes, return it. Otherwise odd and even walk the two chains. Each step pulls the next odd node forward and leaves the evens linked. Attaching the even head after the last odd node produces the grouped list without changing the order inside either chain.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def odd_even_list(head: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    class Node:
        def __init__(self, value: int, nxt=None):
            self.value = value
            self.nxt = nxt

    dummy = Node(0)
    tail = dummy
    for value in head:
        tail.nxt = Node(value)
        tail = tail.nxt
    if dummy.nxt is None or dummy.nxt.nxt is None:
        return head[:]
    odd = dummy.nxt
    even = odd.nxt
    even_head = even
    while even and even.nxt:
        odd.nxt = even.nxt
        odd = odd.nxt
        even.nxt = odd.nxt
        even = even.nxt
    odd.nxt = even_head
    out = []
    node = dummy.nxt
    while node:
        out.append(node.value)
        node = node.nxt
    return out
